CONFIDENCE: 0.78
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the characteristic pattern of a fully chlorinated conjugated diene (hexachlorobutadiene): two strong C=C stretching bands at 1613 cm⁻¹ and 1567 cm⁻¹ (antisymmetric / symmetric modes of the C=C–C=C system), a medium band at 1171 cm⁻¹ assigned to C=C–Cl coupled stretching, a strong out-of-plane mode at 855 cm⁻¹ typical for CCl₂-substituted vinyl groups, and two C–Cl stretching bands at 658 cm⁻¹ and 586 cm⁻¹ (rule GFQ-046 range 652–692 cm⁻¹). Hexachloro-1,3-butadiene, SMILES ClC(Cl)=C(Cl)C(Cl)=C(Cl)Cl (candidate 7), contains no X–H bonds (absence of >3000 cm⁻¹ bands) and matches all observed peaks, whereas candidates with nitrile, carbonyl or nitro groups would require strong bands near 2250 cm⁻¹ or 1700–1800 cm⁻¹ that are not present.
